I think we have fundamentally different views on what makes good documentation. To me, shaping as clear and consistent a mental model of what the function/class does, so users of any knowledge level have the same expectations on how it works, how it can be used and what it returns is the highest priority. If the documentation raises any questions it does not answer, does not prevent common mistakes or causes the user to create bugs (due to them having the wrong expectations after having read the documentation), I consider that a failing of the documentation. After all, where else can users expect to find a reliable source for this information, if not the documentation? While being as concise as possible is obviously important, I would personally never prioritise that over adding additional clarity, especially for an Engine that has become so popular with casual and beginning developers and users that have little to no scripting background.

But if these are the standards and limitation that the Godot Engine has set for it's documentation, then I understand that my changes will have to conform as well. I can only hope that these standards get revised in the future to allow for more comprehensive and approachable documentation!

If you'd be willing to make suggestions that would be better and less verbose in your eyes, I'll accept them.
